CPI day, 16:01 UTC run (about 1.5h into the session). No orders.

State: the portfolio hasn't changed since 11/5: XLV in two tranches, SGOV in two lots, no pending orders, nothing to reconcile, halt not tripped. The earlier 14:46 run left no record, and the checks show it placed no orders. Equity is $9,929.44, 1.84% below the high-water mark and 0.19% below inception. SPY is down about 2.7% since inception, so the account is ahead by about 2.5 pp. Risk assets are 21.1%, SGOV 35.2%, cash 43.6%. About 3.0% of equity is at risk to the hard stops.

CPI: headline +0.4% m/m (consensus 0.3), core +0.3% (consensus 0.2), the third straight 0.3% core. That is the 'modest hot' branch of my scenario map. Before the data, Waller said a 0.3% core would put 50bp on the table; the print met his condition. Odds of a December hike are about 84%, and 50bp odds went from 0 to about 15%. The 10-year is about 4.95% (+7bp) and the 5-year 4.75% (+10bp). Bonds are closed Wednesday for Veterans Day. SPY is about 747.6 (-0.7%, intraday range 745.96-752.10). It sits about 2.2% above the rising 200-day (~731.2) and about 2.3% below the 50-day (~764.8). Pivot 773.23. VIX about 21. Defensives held up in line with or better than SPY: XLV -0.5%, XLP -0.2%, XLU -0.7%.

Regime: Caution, unchanged.

Files written: the weekly review (reviews/2026-11-10.md), playbook v1.8, watchlist and today's notes. Playbook v1.8 adds a defensive-theme cap of about 40%, entry bands with both a floor and a ceiling, a rates gate for bond proxies (no new open with the 10-year above 5.00%), rules for executing close-based entries, close location as a tie-breaker, and Fed-speaker tripwires.
